blocker.reason: Truth is hto12$assign_rna (RNA cell-line calls incl. 'Doublet_rna') read from hto12_processed.rds in deMULTIplex2-benchmark@ac0fa17 Stoeckius_4celline_benchmarking.R; the script says only 'obtained following the Seurat tutorial', which has no assign_rna. The labels are in neither GitHub nor Zenodo 8429628 (code only) nor GEO GSE108313 (count matrices only). A marker-based RNA reconstruction attempted here did not separate HEK293T cleanly and was discarded rather than scored.

Public but needs recomputation: truth = vireo donor_ids.tsv from cellranger + vireo run by the authors on GEO/SRA GSE108313 PBMC FASTQs (Stoeckius_8donor_benchmarking.R line 3); not deposited. Needs cellranger + GRCh38 + cellSNP/vireo on raw reads; not run in this session (cluster queue saturated by other jobs). vireo is unsupervised, so a rerun would not reproduce the authors' labels exactly.

Public but needs recomputation: truth = souporcell clusters.tsv from the authors' run on the GSE161329 RNA reads (McGinnis_8donor_benchmarking_MULTI.R line 20); not deposited. Needs cellranger + souporcell on SRA FASTQs; not run in this session.
Same souporcell truth as ts3_mcginnis_multi (GSE161329 RNA reads, authors' souporcell output not deposited); not run in this session.

analyses.title: deMULTIplex2 F-score, lung cancer cell line

claim.quote: Lung cancer cell line deMULTIplex2 average F-score 0.88

blocker.reason: Tag->tumor table PDX_MULTI-SEQ_Metadata.csv (read in Winkler_PDX_benchmarking.R) is not deposited: GEO GSE211145 has barcode counts + metadata only; the GEO metadata's paper calls pair just 6 of the 15 batch-3 tags (Bar7-Bar15 unmapped) and 2 of 9 batch-2 tags, so the F-score cannot be computed faithfully. Winkler et al. is an unpublished bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2022.08.04.502697) with no supplementary mapping.
Same missing tag->tumor table as ts3_winkler_pdx (PDX_MULTI-SEQ_Metadata.csv, not in GEO GSE211145 / GitHub / Zenodo 8429628); 'correct' = tumor-of-called-tag == expression Tumor_ID needs it.

claim.quote: deMULTIplex2 was able to correctly retrieve the highest number of real singlets (63.2% of all cells) compared to deMULTIplex (50.8% of all cells)
deMULTIplex2 was the only method that maintained its top performance across these simulations (Fig. 2B heatmap, deMULTIplex2 row: F = 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.99, 0.87 for Simulations 1-5)
